shortDescription: Stacks up to 7 playable z-levels (3 up / 3 down) into ONE banded RimWorld Map joined by synthetic RegionLink wormholes, so hauling, needs, work and storage come free from vanilla. Levels and per-level size are bought from a fixed 146,000-cell budget. Per-colony climate bands make high levels genuinely alpine. Content on lower levels draws smaller once per level of drop, which is what makes a deep column read as depth.
body:
# As above, So below II (V2)

> V1 is DELETED. ~70 files, ~20,000 LOC. No em-dashes anywhere in shipped text; keep it that way.

## Pitch
Up to seven z-levels in ONE RimWorld `Map`. Priorities in order: (1) visual clarity from above, (2) performance, (3) vanilla parity.

## Status
Visuality, QOL, altitude/weather and settings passes are all VERIFIED IN PLAY. **Seven-level maps generate clean: 4.1 s for 7 bands (run #207), 3.2 s for 4 bands (run #206).** UNVERIFIED IN PLAY: below-snow, the depth shrink (§6g), the new-game camera anchor (§8a), the whole §18 audit, and the Map Preview reroll grid (§6d-REROLL).

---

# 1. ARCHITECTURE
One `Map`, size `(w, 1, bandCount * Slot)`. Bands stack along +z from the deepest basement, with a permanently-fogged gutter between them. `Slot = ceil((bandHeight+2)/64)*64`; **64-alignment is load-bearing** (terrain shaders sample by world position). Per-level sizes 126 / 190 / 254.

**The one insight.** `Region.Neighbors` is *topological, not spatial*. Wormhole `RegionLink`s between one-cell `RegionType.Portal` ends conduct connectivity without merging rooms, temperature or vacuum, and `Reachability.CanReach` works unpatched. But reachability is not a path: 1.6's pathfinder is jobified and cannot traverse a synthetic link, hence segmented movement (§3).

**Hard 1.6 constraints.** The path grid is an IJobParallelFor over EVERY cell, so total stacked cells is the runtime metric. No `PathFinder.FindPath`. `BlocksDiagonalMovement` trips on unwalkable cells.

**⚠ The stack is 2x to 7x anisotropic.** Anything vanilla normalises by BOTH map dimensions is distorted, and that bug class cannot appear on an ordinary square map.

### ⚠ THE SLICING RULE, six shapes
| Shape | Example | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| Anchor, a point picked as a fraction of `Size.z` | river and lake centre; random/edge cell (§15a) | remap the point |
| Field, a gradient centred on the map centre | coastline (§6e) | re-centre the sample coordinate |
| Noise space, a slice is not a short map | Map Preview (§6d) | generate at full height, then crop |
| Distance-to-extent, a margin measured off `Size` | `CloseToEdge`, no-build edge (§15b, §15d) | re-base onto the cell's own band rect |
| **Aspect ratio, normalised by BOTH dims** | preview window AND reroll grid (§6d) | lay out from the BAND, generate at the STACK |
| **Map-wide scalar**, one per-tick value for the whole map | snow melt (§7), temperature readout (§16) | rewrite it per cell at the consumer |

Classify a new bug into one of these six, but PROVE it. Still unaudited: Basin, Cavern, Chasm, Cliffs, Hollow, Valley (all use `FalloffAtAngle`).

# 2. LEVEL PLAN, budget 146,000 cells, FIXED
`4 x 190 = 145,920` sets the figure. `5 x 190` and `3 x 254` are refused. `ABMapSizeLimit` owns it. **`7 x 126 = 112,896` is VERIFIED IN PLAY (runs #196, #207).**
Per-level size is SQUARE, which is why `GenStep_Scatterer.CountFromPer10kCells` (it squares `Size.x`, not `map.Area`) already yields a per-BAND count. Only `GenStep_AnimaTrees` and `GenStep_TerrainPatches` read `map.Area`.

**⚠ The level chooser is also the lab.** `0 above / 0 below` generates an ORDINARY single-level map, the vanilla control. **STILL UNVERIFIED: does `0 up / 0 down` actually reach generation?**

**⚠ The chooser UI: own the widget, do not patch the data.** `Dialog_AdvancedGameConfig.MapSizes` is `static readonly` and the reflection swap SILENTLY FAILED in play. Now our own radio buttons write `mapSize` directly. Window grown via an `InitialSize` postfix.
**⚠ The chooser LATCHES global state, and the release is a `Finalizer`.** `BeginChooser` sets `inChooser` (which gates a patch on `Listing_Standard.RadioButton`, a primitive every mod's settings window uses) and swaps the static `MapSizes` array. That release used to sit in the Postfix's `finally`, which does not run when VANILLA throws - see §18a.
**The level spinners are NOT known to be broken.** Run #190's "wrong plan" was USER ERROR, confirmed. **The plan PERSISTS between colonies**, which is the likeliest explanation for any future report.

# 3. CROSS-BAND MOVEMENT
Segmented at ONE interception: `StartPath` prefix, tick sweep, `Carry` re-issues `StartPath`. `ABWormhole.TryGetTransit` BFSes the band graph; hops must strictly decrease. **Multi-hop routing STILL UNTESTED IN PLAY.**

# 4. GROUP ORDERING
`RecomputeDestinations` spreads the selection along the drag line, which between bands runs through the GUTTER. The odd/even signature ("3 and 5 fail, 2 and 4 do not") is the proof, because only ODD counts sample exactly 0.5. Fix normalises `start`/`end` into the commanded pawns' band. Verified.

# 5. ⚠ ONE DESCENT RULE: `ABBands.TryResolveVisibleBelow`
Descends while each level is see-through, stops at the first opaque floor or the bottom band, returns the accumulated drop. TEN systems share it. **EIGHT separate appearances of the single `- Slot` bug** (the eighth found by the §18 audit, in the lighting overlay, written as INDEX arithmetic so the standing `grep '- Slot'` audit could not see it).

**`ABBands.TryResolveVisibleFrom` is now THE gate**, and it is what most consumers should call. It folds the four-question preamble every caller was hand-rolling - in bounds, band > 0, out of the gutter, own terrain see-through - onto the descent, plus an optional unfogged check. Six passes are on it (lighting, snow, watergen, sun shadows, edge shadows, click-through). Two legitimate exceptions: `SectionLayer_ABBelowV2` needs the "in bounds but fogged" distinction to emit its air mask and fog fan, and the upward-shape consumers (`ABBelowDynamicDraw`, `ABBelowOverlays`, `ABBelowMultiSelect`, `ABBelowSelectionDraw`) ask a different question - "is THIS thing what the column shows" - and translate before descending.

Sun-shadow subtlety: its mask is neighbour-based, so mask and descent are answered together by `TryResolveDropAround`, taking the smallest drop among the nine cells.
Still single-band AND unshrunk: the realtime-things pass in `ABBelowDynamicDraw` (motes, fire, frames, projectiles).

# 6. SKY-MASS PRESENTATION (verified)
Four rejected attempts on record: force-linked wall masks, high-queue cover, wall-sprite suppression, and theorising twice about "flat" mountains before running the below-layer report.
Despeckle (walls dissolve only at 7+ open neighbours; at 6 it ate the outermost wall row off every meadow edge), one central fog hole, five-terrain plateau palette, cliff faces, alpine pass.
**⚠ The mass tapers with altitude, so +3 may contain NO LAND AT ALL.** Check for ground before diagnosing anything about the top level. Confirmed by timing in §9e and again in #207 (`Sky clear` 41.6 / 6.7 / 7.7 ms).
Ore glyph bug: ore defs have no `naturalTerrain`, so a "can't happen" fallback drew the whole atlas sheet per cell.

# 6a. ⚠ THE BELOW VIEW IS A SET OF MIRRORED PASSES, NOT ONE RENDERER
`SectionLayer_ABBelowV2` is a faithful port of vanilla `SectionLayer_Terrain` **and nothing else**. Every OTHER vanilla pass that contributes to how ground looks needs its own mirror, or that contribution is simply absent from the below view. Confirmed twice: **Water** (§6b) and **Snow** (§6f).
Before adding a below-view feature, ask which vanilla SectionLayer draws it. Existing mirrors: BelowV2 (terrain + things + fog fan), BelowLighting, BelowShadows, BelowEdgeShadows, BelowWatergen, BelowSnow, MountainCap.

**Cross-band invalidation is solved by `Patch_MapDrawer_ABMirrorDirtyUp`, and it now obeys an ASCENT RULE.** It mirrors every dirty flag verbatim to bands above, so a new mirrored layer costs one `relevantChangeTypes` line rather than a new propagation path. **But it used to climb to EVERY band unconditionally, and that is the inverse of §5.** A band can only show a cell if every level between them is see-through; the first opaque floor hides it from that band and all above. The climb now stops there, tested over the cell AND its eight neighbours (the mirrored passes are neighbour-sampling: edge fades, fog fan, snow kernel, shadow caster mask). The FIRST step stays unconditional because `SectionLayer_ABMountainCap` derives from exactly one Slot below regardless of transparency. The patch also mirrors vanilla's own `ProgramState != Playing` guard - see §18b.

**⚠ THE UNIT OF WASTE HERE IS A SECTION REGENERATION, NOT A CELL.** Seven of our layers plus vanilla's ten rebuild per dirtied section, so an unbounded mirror multiplied every mined rock by bandCount. Steady-state fps never showed it; it lands entirely in the hitches during mining and construction.

**⚠ SIX PASSES SHARE THE BELOW VIEW.** Any future per-frame geometry transform must be applied to ALL of them from one definition, or lighting / shadow / water / snow shear off the terrain they belong to. That coupling is what made Perspective Mode expensive to own (§6g).

# 6b. ⚠ WATER: 1.6 water is a TWO-PASS SCREEN-SPACE effect
`SectionLayer_Watergen` (vanilla, `internal`, cannot be subclassed) is `SectionLayer_Terrain` plus `waterDepthMaterial`, drawn to the WaterDepth SUBCAMERA's layer. The visible `Map/TerrainWater` material samples that texture at its own SCREEN position.
- Water missing from upper levels, FIXED: `SectionLayer_ABBelowWatergen` overrides `DrawLayer` to target `SubcameraDefOf.WaterDepth.LayerId`.
- Rivers not generating, FIXED: remap `GetRiverCenter` (not `Init`, which consumes it immediately). `GetLakeCenter` needs the same patch or it undoes the first.

# 6b-LAKE. CLOSED: surface streaking accepted as vanilla appearance
PROVEN in run #173: a tile with water but no water mutators still streaked. **The ghost-river theory is dead; do not revive it.** Found en route: vanilla's flow builder ends `zero /= (float)num3` with no zero guard, writing NaN into a bilinear-filtered texture.

# 6c. DUBS MINT MINIMAP (verified)
ONE RECT, not seven patches. `DrawTextureFitted` preserves the TEXTURE's aspect, so use `ScaleMode.StretchToFill`. Reflection only.

# 6d. MAP PREVIEW (m00nl1ght.MapPreview)
Never calls `MapGenerator.GenerateMap` - it builds a bare Map and runs a short genstep list on a background thread. So our banding prefix never fires. **Generate at the full stacked height and crop via `TexCoords`**, because the surface band is a SLICE of a taller noise field and rows 384-510 of a 190x768 map bear no relation to rows 0-189 of a 190x190 one. `MaxMapSize.z` MUST rise (default 500, a stack reaches 896). Most of it uses their public hooks (`MapSizeUtility.MaxMapSize`, `MapSizeOverride`), not Harmony.

## 6d-REROLL. THE SEED REROLL GRID (UNVERIFIED IN PLAY)
Their seed reroll (OFF by default in their settings) opens `MapSeedRerollWindow`, a grid of candidate previews.

**The seed itself needs NOTHING from us, and that is worth knowing before touching it.** Preview seeds come from `MapPreviewRequest.SeedFromWorldSeed` -> `SeedRerollData.GetMapSeed`; the real map's seed is adjusted by a TRANSPILER on `MapGenerator.GenerateMap` inserting `AdjustSeedIfNeeded` right after `Gen.HashCombineInt`. Same store, both sides, and we never touch the seed - so preview and committed map already agree, rerolled or not. Our prefix only changes SIZE, which is orthogonal.

**⚠ WHAT WAS BROKEN: the window opened COMPLETELY EMPTY.** `PreOpen` correctly takes the STACKED size from `DetermineMapSize` (necessary - thumbnails must generate at stacked height or their noise would not match). But `UpdateElementSize` then shapes each thumbnail as `y = width / mapSize.x * mapSize.z` and derives the row count from it:
```
126x896 stack, 2560px window, 6 per row
  elementSize.y = 403 / 126 * 896 = 2,866 px   (a 7:1 sliver)
  gridSize.y    = floor(1330 / 2886) = 0
  DesiredCount  = 0  ->  trim loop disposes every element
  TryAddElement -> `if (_elements.Count >= DesiredCount) return;` -> 0 >= 0 -> returns
```
Nothing is ever queued. **This is the SECOND consumer of the stacked size caught out by it** - the first was their main preview window (`FixWindowAspect`) - and it is the aspect-ratio row of the slicing rule.

Fixed by `Patch_MapPreview_ABRerollGrid`, a postfix on `UpdateElementSize` that re-derives `_elementSize.y` from the BAND height, recomputes `_gridSize.y`, and kicks `TryAddElement` once (its promise chain self-feeds). A POSTFIX repairing two statics, not a prefix reimplementing the method: their width maths and trim loop are correct, and a reimplementation would drift on their next update.
- **Rejected: suppressing our inflation while the reroll window is open.** Simpler, and it would make every thumbnail a picture of a map that will never generate.
- **Cropping is free here:** `MapPreviewWidget.OnPromiseResolved` copies `result.TexCoords` and `DrawGenerated` draws through it, so the existing `CropTexCoords` patch already trims each thumbnail to the surface band.
- **Accepted cost:** each Element allocates a `Texture2D` at the STACKED size (~451 KB at 126x896), up to ~60 in a grid, so roughly 27 MB of which 6/7 is cropped away. Left alone on the user's call - it is transient (only while the window is open) and shrinking it would mean overriding `MapPreviewRequest.TextureSize` and keeping the crop consistent, roughly doubling the patch surface against a mod that updates.
- `_elementSize` / `_gridSize` are STATIC, so a second open skips `UpdateElementSize` entirely and reuses the corrected values. Harmless. On an ordinary map `TryBandRows` refuses the size and their own arithmetic (already correct) stands.

# 6e. COASTS (verified)
CENTRED wrong, not scaled wrong. `z' = (z % Slot) + (map.Size.z - bandHeight) / 2`, NO SCALING. Nine coastal mutators, none override `GetNoiseValue`.

# 6f. BELOW-SNOW (`SectionLayer_ABBelowSnow.cs`, UNVERIFIED IN PLAY)
Snow lying on a lower level was invisible from above. Not masking, not translation, not the descent rule: **no mirror of `SectionLayer_Snow` existed**, so below-snow was never emitted.
**The near-miss that hid it:** `CellTerrainAt` genuinely samples `map.snowGrid.GetDepth(below)` from the correct cell, but `CellTerrain`'s snow coverage is consumed only by `MaterialFor`, to pick the POLLUTED terrain variant. The right value was read for an entirely different purpose.
**Why it was simpler than the terrain mirror:** vanilla's snow layer emits no per-cell geometry - ONE solid 9-verts-per-cell grid over the section, only vertex COLOURS rewritten, depth in alpha. That grid is positional and our section already sits in the viewing band, so only the sampled cells move. No vertex fix-up, no `- Slot`.
Details: geometry built once and reused (NOT `ClearSubMeshes(All)`, unlike every other AB layer, or colour count stops matching vertex count); iteration order must match `MakeBaseGeometry` (x outer, z inner, nine per cell); cells with nothing below still emit nine transparent vertices or all later colours shift; altitude matches the below-terrain print (`TerrainScatter`); all nine kernel samples taken at the CENTRE cell's drop, because mixing two bands into one smoothing kernel would seam.
**⚠ Open risk:** draw ordering is queue-decided. `MatBases.Snow` may need queue work. Expect one iteration, as water did.

# 6g. DEPTH SHRINK (`ABDepthView.cs`, UNVERIFIED IN PLAY)
The below view was geometrically correct and read as **flat levels stacked in a list**. Restores V1's `belowThingScale`, generalised: the exponent is the accumulated drop from `TryResolveVisibleBelow` (three levels down draws at 61%). Baked into vertices at print time, hence free per frame. DEFAULT ON, slider 60-100%.
- **Printed things:** `FinishNewVerts` does shrink-about-`TrueCenter` and the `drop` translate in ONE pass, scale first, so the pivot is the real centre.
- **Live pawns:** `Patch_PawnRenderer_ABBelowShrink` right-multiplies `PawnDrawParms.matrix`. Right-multiply is load-bearing (local space); a left multiply slides every below pawn towards the map origin.
- **⚠ The atlas trap:** past `ZoomRootSize` 18 humanlikes render from a cached atlas blit that never reads `PawnDrawParms.matrix`, so the scale silently evaporates at exactly the zooms used to look down a column. `Patch_PawnRenderer_ABBelowDisableCache` forces `disableCache` for below pawns only. **Verification must cross that boundary in both directions.**
- **⚠ V1's exclusion filter kept verbatim, both halves paid for:** LINKED graphics print one quad per cell, so per-cell shrink dots a wall into a dashed line; natural rock is excluded BY DEF (`mineable` / `isNaturalRock`) not by link type, because Better Mountains swaps rock to non-linked `Graphic_Random` wholesale (V1 run #50).
- Baked, so a settings change needs `RegenerateEverythingNow` - once in `ABMod.WriteSettings`, not per slider frame.
- **Not tinted.** `SectionLayer_ABBelowLighting` already shades below content; a tint on top is the double-darkening that made V1's sky view murky.

**⚠ PERSPECTIVE MODE WAS BUILT AND REMOVED. Do not re-add it as polish.** A camera-anchored contraction (`p' = eye + (p - eye) / (1 + k)`) as a per-frame `Matrix4x4`, mirroring vanilla's own `MapDrawLayer_OrbitalDebris`. It worked and was cheap. Cut on the user's call once the shrink was seen in play: the shrink alone already carried the depth read, and perspective bought a second cue at the price of a real artifact (no occlusion exists between a band's floor and the level below, so content slid out from under the near lip towards the screen edges). Re-opening needs a NEW reason and must re-solve the six-pass coupling in §6a.

# 7. PER-LEVEL CHARACTER
Ore `x(1 + 0.45*(depth-1))`, cave openness `x(1 + 0.35*(depth-1))`, both applied AFTER the settings clamp.
**⚠ The snow line never worked, and the comment saying it did not need to was wrong.** `SteadyEnvironmentEffectsTick` computes `outdoorMeltAmount` once per tick for the whole map and never calls `TryGetTemperatureForCell`. Dead for months behind a confident, wrong sentence.
**Climate defaults** (per colony, §17): +1 = -7, +2 = -16, +3 = -35, basement flat -6, wind x1.15 / x1.30 / x1.50. **No ceiling clamp by design.**

# 8. CAMERA
`ABCameraBounds.For(level)` keyed by LEVEL, not band index. `maxZoom` left DERIVED. `panMargin` 63.5 on every level. `Dialog_ABCameraCalibration` opens with the clamp UNLOCKED.
**The clamp and the level-switch input share `ABGuard.Camera`.** Both sit on per-frame / per-GUI-event paths, which is exactly where an unthrottled `Log.Error` turns a cosmetic bug into an unplayable game (§18a). Consequence: if the clamp trips, band switching stops too. The view clip and the curtain are NOT gated on it, so other bands stay hidden either way.

# 8a. NEW-GAME CAMERA ANCHOR (`ABBandView.LandOnColony`, UNVERIFIED IN PLAY)
`Game.InitNewGame` ends with `JumpToCurrentMapLoc(MapGenerator.PlayerStartSpot)`. Correct on an ordinary map because nothing moves the colony after the spot is chosen. On a banded map two things do, BOTH after the pawns are on the ground: `RescueStrandedColonists` relocates anything the pod scatter threw across a gutter, and the carve can make the recorded spot unstandable.
**Confirmed mechanism in run #200:** `DropThingsNear failed to find a place to drop Nyx near (153, 0, 24). Dropping on random square instead.`
Fixed in two places: **upstream**, `FixPlayerStartSpot` prefers the colony's ACTUAL position (free colonist nearest the centroid, restricted to the surface band); **backstop**, `ABGameComp.StartedNewGame` calls `LandOnColony`. **⚠ That hook, and only that hook, runs after vanilla's own camera jump** - a `GameComponent.FinalizeInit` hook is overwritten a few lines later. `rememberedCameraPos` is written by hand too, or the load-path fixer would undo it.
**⚠ OPEN, NOT YET DISTINGUISHED:** in #200 the start spot was `z=24` on a band spanning 0-189, EXACTLY the `PodScatterMargin = 24` boundary. Vanilla's own pick landing there and my clamp pinning it there look IDENTICAL from outside. Verbose logging prints both; run one colony with it on before touching the margin.

# 9. GENERATION COST: DIAGNOSED AND LARGELY FIXED

## 9a. The profile stamps its own conditions
`ABGenProfile.Report` prints `TILE`, `PLAN`, a `SCOPING:` toggle line, and two censuses (`DESTROYED by def`, `SUPPRESSED by def`). Added because four earlier carve timings lacked the tile and are uninterpretable. It caught a changed tile on its FIRST use and voided a comparison that would otherwise have been believed. Emitted at WARNING level deliberately: single-occurrence info is filtered before it reaches the monitor.

## 9b. ⚠ THE COST IS DESTRUCTION, NOT GENERATION
Run #188: gensteps 3,972 ms, carve 20,447 ms (98.4% of it `Sky clear`), 74,584 things destroyed. Generation is 16%, destruction 84%. **The original "scoping saves both halves" framing was WRONG.** Per-destroy price is stable across runs and tiles, so **op count is the only lever**. Mechanism is `ListerThings` removal, a linear `List.Remove` over ~100k-item lists.
**CLOSED:** carving before `FinalizeInit` is worth at most 169 ms of 24,600.

## 9c. The culprit was rock, proven by census
Run #190: 43,517 rock SUPPRESSED vs 4,939 DESTROYED of which only 238 rock. Reproduced on tiles 2, 3 and 4 (#200, #205, #206). The ratio is stable across four tiles and three biomes.

## 9d. SHIPPED: `ABDoomedBands.cs`
Suppresses `GenSpawn.Spawn(ThingDef,...)` inside `GenStep_RocksFromGrid` for doomed SKY band cells. Safe because: **shape** (per-cell noise test, no count redistributed); **state-neutrality** (only the spawn is cancelled - roofs, roof cleanup and `ScatterLumpsMineable` all still run, and `ClearCellHard` never touched roofs); **sky only**. Patched on the `ThingDef` overload so the cancel precedes `ThingMaker.MakeThing`.

## 9e. Run #196: the first basement, and the bottleneck moved
7 bands, 126x896. FillRock bands 0-2 = 2,606 ms (82% of carve); Sky clear = 301 ms (9%). **The sky side is solved. The basement is the whole cost.**
**⚠ MY OWN §9d CAUTION IS FALSIFIED.** I argued against suppressing vanilla rock in basement bands because `FillRock` keeps it. The keep hits only **14.4%** of the time. Suppressing trades 7,113 destroys (~1.4 s) for 6,873 extra spawns (~200 ms), because destroys cost roughly 7x spawns inside the generation window. **Net ~1.2 s.** The shape of the reasoning was right; the magnitude was never checked, because no basement had ever run.
**Sign flip, a confirmation not a bug:** with rock suppressed, `Sky clear` per band INVERTED (rising with altitude). Rock tapers upward, so higher bands have more OPEN ground, and chunks only grow on open ground. Confirmed again in #200, #205, #206, #207.
**Do not blanket-skip** water or coast mutators; §6b, §6e, §6d depend on them.

## 9f. Post-audit numbers (runs #205-#207)
Against the closest matched runs, carve time fell and the per-destroy cost dropped into the documented band:

| | pre-audit | post-audit |
|---|---|---|
| 4-band BorealForest carve | 1,243 ms (#200) | 1,108 ms (#206) |
| ms per destroy | 0.325 | 0.243 / 0.227 |
| 7-band FillRock | 2,606 ms (#196) | 1,911 ms (#207), -27% |
| 7-band total | ~5.5 s | **~4.1 s** |

**⚠ NOT PROVEN, and the confound is stated:** every comparison crosses tiles and biomes, and #207 spawned MORE rock (41,399 vs 40,755) while destroying LESS (5,913 vs 7,113) - destroys cost ~7x spawns, so some of the gain is tile luck. **And the `ScatterOres` allocation fix cannot explain it** (~190 KB/band is worth a millisecond, not 695). The plausible mechanism is the mirror `ProgramState` guard: `FillRock` issues ~95k `MapMeshDirty` calls and the old mirror ran its full loop on every one (it used `continue`, never `break`). A clean number needs the same tile with the guard toggled.

## 9g. Next targets, ranked
1. **Basement rock suppression** (§9e), ~1.2 s, the largest remaining item.
2. **`GenStep_RockChunks`**, the dominant survivor on sky-only maps (`Filth_RubbleRock` 2,856 of 4,755 in #205, 2,688 of 4,567 in #206). Verified per-cell probabilistic, passes the shape test.
3. **Scattered ruins, also a CONTENT BUG.** Per §2 a scatterer's count is sized for ONE band but placement spans the whole stack, so **the surface is losing a large share of the ruins vanilla intended**. Fixes content and cost together. ⚠ Paired risk: the `could not find cell to generate at` starvation signal has fired on three tiles (#190, #200, #205) but NOT on #206/#207 - it is tile-dependent, not universal.
4. **`ABRockGen.PickIndex` evaluates every rock type's 6-octave Perlin per cell**, ~650k noise samples per 190-band, recomputed for wall cells again in `ABSkyBandGen`. Precompute a `byte[]` rock-index grid per band, or cut the octave count. NOT DONE: it changes generation determinism.

# 10, 11. PERF AND LINKS
59.6 fps at 96 pawns, mod approximately 2% of frame. All rendering is bake-time section-mesh geometry. Elevator SHIPPED but untested.
**⚠ THAT BENCHMARK MEASURES THE WRONG THING, and §18 is why.** This architecture's cost is concentrated in section-regeneration BURSTS, not steady state. A colony standing still never triggers the dirty mirror; a colonist mining a 20x20 room with three sky levels open triggers a section rebuild per band. Any future perf claim needs a mining/construction test with a multi-level plan, watching the frame graph, not the average.

# 12. DIAGNOSTICS
Band info, below layer and pawn reports, water report, transit health, stuck probe, lighting/shader/biome reports, bisect toggles, ABGenProfile, camera calibration.
**⚠ Bisect toggles PERSIST in the pinned palette across runs.** Run #172 opened with a stale `belowWater=False` that mimicked a fixed bug exactly. Scoping toggles are now STAMPED INTO THE PROFILE.
**⚠ Poll the monitor even when nothing auto-prompts.** Single-occurrence `[RimWorld]` warnings are filtered from summaries. Confirmed in #190, #200, #205, #206 and #207 - in #205 the poll turned up both the scatterer starvation AND a failed palette pin, neither of which auto-prompted.
**⚠ The pre-pinned palette always loses its LAST entry.** `Dialog_DevPalette.EnsureAllNodesValid` walks the list BACKWARDS while `Dialog_Debug.GetNode` is still lazily building the node graph, so the last lookup fails, and a miss REMOVES the pin and saves Prefs. Confirmed at n=3 (#205, #206, #207) - the victim changed each time and always sat last. Pad with a DISTINCT throwaway entry; a duplicate does not work because the pin writer deduplicates.
**⚠ The auto-prompt is edge-triggered per run.** Use `monitor_get_error` (returns the LATEST occurrence) or watch the `×count`.
`AB2: band info` is the fastest ground truth for "what did this map actually generate as".
**Kill switches are a diagnostic surface, so every switch must have a call site.** Twelve of nineteen had none (§18c).

# 13. OPEN WORK
1. **Verify the §18 audit in play.** Highest value: the dirty-mirror ascent rule (stale below view would show as "mineables disappear on floor 2") and the lighting descent fix (deep views should now darken at night). Test: 3 sky levels, mine a large surface area, check +1/+2/+3, then check night lighting from +3.
2. **Verify the reroll grid** (§6d-REROLL). Needs Map Preview as a companion AND its reroll feature enabled (OFF by default). Expect: grid populates with square, surface-band thumbnails instead of opening empty.
3. **Verify the depth shrink** (§6g), crossing `ZoomRootSize` 18 in both directions.
4. **Verify the new-game camera anchor** (§8a); separate the two readings of the `z=24` start spot with verbose logging on.
5. **Verify below-snow** (§6f). Queue ordering is the expected failure mode.
6. **Basement rock suppression** (§9e/9g), ~38% of the remaining carve.
7. §9g items 3 and 4 (ruins content deficit; Perlin precompute).
8. **Audit the other `FalloffAtAngle` mutators**: Basin, Cavern, Chasm, Cliffs, Hollow, Valley.
9. **Never exercised in play:** multi-hop stair router, elevator, reload fix. Basement GENERATION verified (#196, #207); basement PATHING and wormholes still are not.
10. **The cavern basement has NEVER been exercised** (§18e). Needs `companionMods: ["BiomesTeam.BiomesCaverns"]`.

# 14. LESSONS
**Method.** Prove a subsystem innocent by finding a state where the suspect CANNOT EXIST. A documented rejection may be re-opened only by naming the confound that invalidated it. Change one thing per experiment. Run the diagnostic before the third theory. An exact number is a diagnosis. Use the product's own knobs as lab equipment. A beautiful fit is not evidence. Knowing when to stop is a result.
**⚠ Measure the ratio before optimising the half you assumed.** Generation was 16%, deletion 84%. The fix was right, the reason was wrong, and only the profile said so.
**⚠ A census beats a magnitude.** "74,584 things" is not a diagnosis; "43,517 Granite and Limestone" is. Pair a SUPPRESSED census with a DESTROYED one so the two are a conservation check.
**⚠ Stamp the experiment's conditions into its own output.** The tile stamp voided a bad comparison on its first run - and then voided three more (#205-#207), every one of which crossed tiles.
**⚠ Evidence consistent with both hypotheses is not evidence; the discriminating experiment is usually cheap.** Three times now. The persisted spinner. The `z=24` start spot. And the palette pin: "that label is broken" and "the last entry is broken" predict different things the moment you REORDER the list, which cost one run to settle after two runs of guessing.
**⚠ An optimisation you declined for a stated reason still owes you the number.** The basement keep was left alone on the reasoning that it saved work; the hit rate was 14.4% and the decision inverted.
**⚠ When a symptom says "X is missing", ask how many PASSES X takes.** Water (two passes, screen-space) and snow (its own SectionLayer).
**⚠ A correct value read for the wrong purpose looks like coverage.** Below-snow was sampled correctly and used only to pick a pollution variant. Grep for the value's CONSUMER, not just its read site.
**⚠ A deleted feature's exclusion list is the expensive part.** Restoring the below shrink was fifteen lines; the value was in the two exclusions and the atlas-cache trap.
**⚠ Two cues for one property is one cue too many.** Perspective Mode was correct, cheap and cut anyway. Build the smaller cue first and check whether it is sufficient BEFORE building the larger one.
**⚠ When two hooks both "run at startup", find the one that runs after the thing you are fixing.**
**⚠ Aim at the fact, not at the record of the intent.** `PlayerStartSpot` is a plan; the pawns are where the colony IS.
**⚠ A rule enforced by grepping for a SYNTAX only catches that syntax.** The descent rule was audited by grepping `- Slot`. Its eighth instance was written as index arithmetic and sailed through every sweep. A rule holds when the correct version is the only CONVENIENT one.
**⚠ Duplication is how an invariant dies.** Seven copies of the see-below preamble, each with a slightly different subset of the checks, is the soil the eighth descent bug grew in.
**⚠ A comment is not an invariant.** "Each callee self-guards" was true of three files and enforced by none.
**⚠ A kill switch with no call site is not a safety net, it is noise.**
**⚠ Steady-state fps hides burst cost.** Benchmark the ACTIVITY that triggers the work, not the idle state.
**⚠ The second consumer of a value you reshaped will not announce itself.** The stacked map size broke their preview window, was fixed, and then broke their reroll grid the same way months later. When you feed a foreign system a value outside the range it expects, grep for EVERY reader of that value, not the one that reported a bug.
**⚠ Timing that reads exactly 0.0 ms is an early return, not slow code.** `CavernGen` looked like a broken feature across two runs; it was an absent optional dependency (§18e). Read the guard clauses before profiling the body.
**⚠ In a foreign log, the loudest error is usually downstream.** The NRE everyone sees in `InitNewGame` was 24 lines and one long-event later than the `ArgumentOutOfRangeException` that actually caused it (§19).
**Claims versus facts.** A comment asserting why something is safe to delete is a claim (§7). Re-measure the assumption you are about to build on. Verify a patched branch is reachable before debugging your own logic.
**Shapes.** Classify into one of the six. A slice of a tall map is not a short map. A uniform symptom is a scale or constant, a patchy one is data. An odd/even symptom is arithmetic.
**Patching.** When N call sites share ONE linear mapping, re-aim the shared parameter. Find the ONE virtual everything funnels through. Patch the method that PRODUCES a value, not the one that stores it. Patch the idempotent READ, not the cached WRITE. Own the widget instead of patching the data it reads. Never put a foreign type in a patch-class signature. **Suppress the callee, not the caller.** **State taken in a Prefix is released in a Finalizer, never a Postfix** (§18a). **Mirror the guard of the method you postfix** (§18b). **Repair a foreign method's output rather than reimplementing its body**, when only part of its maths is wrong (§6d-REROLL).
**Engine facts.** `TerrainDef.holdSnowOrSand` defaults TRUE. Draw order inside and across SectionLayers is settled by material render QUEUE, not by altitude. Altitude is draw order for things, and `WorldClipper` sorts above `Skyfaller`. A null global texture falls back to the shader's default. Vanilla divides by a count without guarding zero. A spatial helper that reaches 22 rows will cross a 2-row gutter. `Banded` is FALSE for the whole of map generation. `SectionLayer` subclasses are auto-discovered by `Section`'s constructor, on EVERY map. Any type with a `Material` field needs `[StaticConstructorOnStartup]`. Statics keyed by game-scoped ids leak; use a CWT. FinalizeInit runs on a worker thread. Ore defs have no `naturalTerrain`. `CameraJumper.TryJump` silently returns unless `ProgramState == Playing`. **`MapDrawer.MapMeshDirty` also returns unless `ProgramState == Playing`.** `MapDrawLayer.DrawLayer` takes a per-submesh matrix. Humanlike pawns past `ZoomRootSize` 18 render from an atlas blit that ignores `PawnDrawParms.matrix`. **Gensteps run with live-map bookkeeping DEFERRED, which is why the same work costs ~40x after `FinalizeInit`.** Harmony skips POSTFIXES when the original throws, but always runs FINALIZERS. **The player's starting settlement is created by `ScenPart_PlayerFaction.PreMapGenerate()`, in a SEPARATE long event from `InitNewGame` - so a throw in the first leaves the second running against a world with no player base.**

# 15. QOL PASS (verified, run #172)
**15a. Nothing may exist in the void.** `ABBandSafety.cs`. Finders answer inside the surface band; a prefix on the 7-arg `GenSpawn.Spawn` rewrites `loc`; a 120-tick sweep catches teleports and pre-fix saves. Always relocates to the SURFACE. Scoped to pawns and the gutter only.
**15b. Structures must not straddle a seam.** `GenGrid.CloseToEdge` measured against `map.Size`, so the surface band reported itself as inland everywhere. One prefix re-bases onto the cell's own band rect; eleven cold call sites inherit it. Backstop: postfix on `GenStep_Scatterer.CanScatterAt`. Seam margin DERIVED (`bandHeight/24`, clamped 4 to 12).
**⚠ ONE surface-edge finder, `ABBandSafety.TryRandomSurfaceEdgeCell(map, Rot4? dir, ...)`.** There were two, in different files behind different helper classes, because the dir and no-dir vanilla overloads were band-corrected at different times. A null dir means "any side, re-rolled every attempt" - preserved deliberately, because a validator that rejects a whole side must not trap the search on it.
**15c.** `panMargin` 63.5 on every level.
**15d. Vanilla's no-build map edge REMOVED on banded maps.** Consequence: vanilla's strip is also what stops a colony sealing its map edge.
**15e. Drop pods fall through the levels.** Suppress `Skyfaller.DrawAt`, re-issue via `DrawNowAt` translated by `(viewedBand - itsBand) * Slot`. Altitude chosen PER FRAME. `Skyfaller_FlyingPawn` excluded.

# 16. ALTITUDE AND WEATHER (`ABBandWeather.cs`, verified)
One weather INTERPRETED per band, since `WeatherManager` is per-Map.
- **Snow confined to real ground:** `AB_OpenAir` and `AB_WallTop` set `holdSnowOrSand=false`.
- **Melt per band:** prefix on `DoCellSteadyEffects` rewrites the private `outdoorMeltAmount` on EVERY call including level 0.
- **Snow must exist before it can persist:** `SeedAltitudeSnow` at generation, seeded from CURRENT temperature. ~35 ms.
- **Rain falls and draws as snow above the line.** Accumulation via the public `AddFallenSnowAt`; vanilla gates on the cached field but takes the amount from the live property. Rejected: swapping `WeatherDef.Worker.overlays`, a global Def shared across maps.
- **No overlays underground**, judged on the viewed band.
- **Wind x1.15 / x1.30 / x1.50, zero underground.** Patched on the `DesiredPowerOutput` getter.
- **Readout:** `GlobalControls.TemperatureString` rebuilt from `TryGetTemperatureForCell`. `MapTemperature.OutdoorTemp` is NEVER reached by it, because outdoor cells still belong to a Room and `Room.Temperature` is a stored field.

**Tabbed scrolling window:** Performance, Visuals, Climate, Sky, Basement, Diagnostics. Hand-drawn tab buttons, not `TabDrawer`. Each tab draws inside a try/catch that renders the exception into the pane.
**⚠ The blank-tab bug.** Scroll-view content height measured from the previous frame's `list.CurHeight` is a SELF-SUSTAINING LATCH without a floor. Fix: `Mathf.Max(list.CurHeight + 16f, inner.height)`. **Adding a tab means growing `viewHeights` too.**
**⚠ Draw the diagnostic OUTSIDE the thing being diagnosed.** A fallback error rendered inside a clipped region is silent, and its silence is not evidence.
**The unlock gate.** The checkbox writes to a LOCAL; `unclampMapSize` only becomes true inside the confirmation callback, so the stored value IS the record that the warning was read.
**Climate SNAPSHOTTED onto `ABBandMap` at generation** (`SnapshotClimate`, scribed, on BOTH carve paths).
**A setting baked into VERTICES needs a rebake on change** (§6g), done once in `ABMod.WriteSettings`.
**Removed settings simply stop being scribed.** Old config files keep unknown keys and RimWorld ignores them.

# 18. CODE AUDIT, 2026-07-31 (ALL UNVERIFIED IN PLAY)
Four read-only passes over ~19.8k LOC. Build clean, 0 warnings. The findings clustered into three shapes, and **all three were rules this codebase already states somewhere else**.

## 18a. STATE TAKEN IN A PREFIX, RELEASED IN A POSTFIX (three instances, all fixed)
Harmony does not run postfixes when the original THROWS.
- `Patch_PawnRenderUtility_ABAimAngle` swaps `Stance_Busy.focusTarg` for the duration of a draw - LIVE COMBAT STATE. One exception inside `DrawEquipmentAndApparelExtras` left a pawn permanently aiming at a band-translated cell. Worse, the prefix opened with `patched = null`, which DISCARDS a pending restore rather than deferring it.
- `Patch_AdvancedGameConfig_ABMapSizeLock` latches `inChooser` and swaps the static `MapSizes` array. A throw in VANILLA's body would relabel and DISABLE unrelated radio buttons across the whole game for the rest of the session.
- Both now release in a `Finalizer`, plus restore-on-entry. Saved to user lore.

**Unthrottled `Log.Error` on a hot path, same family, three instances.** The camera clamp is PER-FRAME; `ABBandInput` runs per GUI event; the wormhole re-arm fires per region rebuild. A bare `Log.Error` there writes one line per frame until Player.log and the frame budget collapse - the logging turns a cosmetic bug into a hang. All three now trip a guard switch.

## 18b. THE MIRROR (largest in-play win)
Two problems, both fixed - mechanism in §6a. No `ProgramState` guard (order of 1.3M dead Harmony dispatches per 7-band carve) and no ascent rule (climbed to every band regardless of whether any could see the changed cell).

## 18c. DEAD AND DUPLICATED
- **12 of 19 kill switches had no call site.** Deleted 11, kept and WIRED `Transit`, added `Camera`.
- **The dev spike layout taxed every map in the game** - a second CWT probe on every `Banded()`/`BandOf()` miss, which is the answer on every quest site and unbanded colony. Now behind a `spikeCount == 0` fast-out.
- **`ClearCellHard` was a second copy of `ClearCellExcept`** with nothing kept.
- **Two surface-edge finders** merged (§15b).
- **Five dead locals and one dead parameter** found by hand after the consolidation; the compiler does not warn on a local assigned from a method call.

## 18d. NOT FIXED, DELIBERATELY
- **Below-pawn drawing is serial and cache-disabled.** Vanilla batches `ParallelPreDraw` into a `ManagedJobParallelFor`; our pass runs all three phases inline on the main thread, AND forces the uncached path for exactly those pawns.
- Realtime-things descent and shrink; Perlin precompute; `ShotReport` target-size loss.

## 18e. CLOSED: "CavernGen did nothing in the basement"
It read 0.5 / 0.0 / 0.0 ms in runs #196 and #207 and looked like a broken feature on a Caves tile. **It is an immediate return: `ABCavernGen.Generate` bails on line three when `BiomesCavernsCompat.Resolve(...)` is null, and Biomes! Caverns is not in the isolated test session's mod list.** The trap: the profile's `mutators: Mountain, Caves` line is the VANILLA TILE MUTATOR, which drives vanilla's surface cave generation and has nothing to do with our cavern basement - two unrelated systems sharing a word, printed one line apart. **Consequence: the cavern basement has never been exercised in any run.**

**⚠ Note for any future A/B on generation timing:** the `ScatterOres` rect overload draws a different NUMBER of `Rand` values than the old list overload, so ore placement for a given seed changed. Maps generated before and after 2026-07-31 are not comparable cell-for-cell.

# 19. FOREIGN-MODLIST DIAGNOSIS (2026-07-31, 910 mods)
"Cannot make a map with my full mod list." **Not us**, and the proof is structural: the NRE is thrown while EVALUATING THE ARGUMENTS to `MapGenerator.GenerateMap` (`settlement.MapGeneratorDef` on a null settlement), so `GenerateMap` is never entered and our prefix cannot run. Confirmed by our log tag appearing 0 times in 19,510 lines when `ABGenProfile.Report` is unconditional.

The real cause was 24 lines earlier and in a different long event:
```
ArgumentOutOfRangeException at Verse.GameInitData.PrepForMapGen()   [IL 0x0000b = the FIRST list access]
  - TRANSPILER Lauriichan.PriorityMaster : DefaultPriorityTranspiler
  - PREFIX     rimworld.erdelf.alien_race.main : PrepForMapGenPrefix
  at RimWorld.PageUtility.<InitGameStart>g__PreLoadAct|1_0()
```
`PreLoadAct` runs `PrepForMapGen()` then `Scenario.PreMapGenerate()`; the throw kills it before `ScenPart_PlayerFaction.PreMapGenerate` reaches `Find.WorldObjects.Add(settlement)`. `InitNewGame` is a SEPARATE queued long event, so it runs anyway against a world with no player base.
The failing line is `startingAndOptionalPawns[startingPawnCount]` guarded by `Count > startingPawnCount`, so **`startingPawnCount` must be negative**. Exactly two mods patch that method and both are named in the frame - a 2-mod bisect, not a 910-mod one.
**Red herrings in that log:** 148x `Could not find player faction` is Colony Dashboard's HTTP server polling `Faction.OfPlayer` at the main menu; the `UnityEngine.InputLegacyModule` FileNotFoundException is harmless ReflectionOnly probing; `[ImageOpt]` and `[Map Designer]` are walls of noise.

## TESTING RULE
`isolated=true`, `quicktest=false` (the level chooser needs the menus; Map Preview doubly so).
Compat tests need the target mod as a companion: Dubs (`dubwise.dubsmintminimap`), Map Preview (`m00nl1ght.MapPreview`), Biomes! Caverns (`BiomesTeam.BiomesCaverns`), VQE Ancients (`vanillaquestsexpanded.ancients`).
**Map Preview's reroll feature is OFF by default in its settings** - enable it before testing §6d-REROLL.
Water tests need a river or lake tile, coastline tests a coastal one. **Read the TILE line before comparing two runs.**
**Re-check the level strip before generating.** The plan persists between colonies.
Read the bisect line before trusting any water or snow observation.
Depth-shrink tests need a populated level BELOW the viewing level, and must cross `ZoomRootSize` 18.
**Perf tests must exercise the ACTIVITY, not the idle state** (§11).
**Pad the pinned palette with a distinct throwaway entry** - the last one is always stripped (§12).
